summary: Helped participants occur as zero-marked NPs (builders, uncle), l-series pronominal recipients, or omitted recoverable participants. The activity is commonly b-marked; no experiencer pattern is forced onto the helper/assisted relation.
Reciprocal ḥḏoḏe is an overt object of active help, including collective u+ʕamo with singular agreement. gmiʕawən in MAC Ishaq Material culture/61 supplies distinct Detransitive evidence.

Infectum-wa ranges from repeated labour and governance to a counterfactual protasis (Hors 1/85, already EL85). Unprefixed Infectum includes prospective/conditional and optative assistance; translated past tense alone cannot reclassify it.
m-less Imperativ ʕawalli and plural ʕAwenullan occur across MAC and Prym–Socin beside inherited mʕawən. n+l assimilation and 1sg mʕawannux are preserved, not normalized.

ʕewono/ʕEwono denotes the action of helping; faluṫa is a community labour institution defined by unpaid reciprocal work. This does not create a separate sense of help or a new light-verb construction under ʕwn.
Reader counts of five existing Infectum examples are not supported by the input, which contains four. Actual parsed examples determine the filling quota.
Compact records without verses remain provisional; shared-verse compact forms such as 69/445 and PrS85/101 were checked against the full nearby verse. No verse-less record was quoted.

All 64 records reviewed, including 60 full verses and four compact records with no verse. The compact forms at 2.1/9,2.7/1854,4.I/130,4.II/872 remain provisional no_add decisions and provide no quoted evidence.

Round 1 brings Preterit to five, Infectum to six, Infectum-wa to five, Imperativ to four, Part act. to five and Infinitiv to three (single-sense inherited null example labels counted as 1). Reader claims of two Preterit examples and one Infinitiv example omit those additions.

Opposite roles are indexed by superficially similar l-shaped endings: mʕawanlox at 3.40/1143,1147 refers to Aziz as helper with overt i dawle/noše objects; mʕawnilox at 3.39/1114 marks him as assisted person. Double sequences mʕawanlelan/lellxu and contracted mʕawanallan/allalan require person-by-person checking.

Helping is socially broad but semantically stable: communal kiln labour (1.16/688,695), funeral food (1.15/589), institutional advocacy and liturgy. Active ḥḏoḏe reciprocity and social cooperation do not independently strengthen round-1 Detransitive 1; no secure new Detransitive token occurs here.

Historically framed kəmʕawən at 3.10/106 is Infectum; a translated past cannot turn it into Preterit. mʕawnənne at 1.4/74 is left provisionally Infectum, with an explicit morphology question. -wa suffix sequences at 1.16/688 and 1.42/1849 need paradigm comparison.
The full m-prefixed mʕawnili request is selected for its unusual form, not to fill the already four-example Imperativ cell. -li remains singular even with plural speakers in the quotation frame.
All quoted English is supplied machine translation. Allegations signalled by goya, negative questions and conditional assistance remain speaker-framed; no historical factual claims are inferred.
Confirm the Detransitive paradigm of miʕawən from MAC Ishaq Material culture/61; this proposal rests on one attestation.
At MAC NE Farrucke/4 confirm reduced feminine Imperativ ʕawalli, including any gender-neutral shape versus loss of a feminine ending.
At PrS34/103 determine the segmentation of mʕawanne and the l-marked women as helpers; preserve the source wording while the agent/recipient clitics remain uncertain.
At MAC Ishaq Material culture/61 the edition says twelve where ʕəsri means twenty. Verify the number without silently correcting the edition.
Talay1/143 has w kul where inherited LB143 has d-kul; verify the original source before a fix-text correction.

Confirm Preterit-wa mʕawanwolle at 1.42/1849 versus Infectum-wa with an object suffix; compare mʕawanwonne (1.16/688), mʕawanwola (1.59/2884), and ordinary mʕawniwonne. The proposed new box remains subject to this morphological check.
Is mʕawnənne at 1.4/74 an unprefixed Infectum or contracted Preterit? Recover the four missing compact verses before independently accepting their analyses.
At 2.10/2223, what is the addressee number/gender of mʕawnili after singular gdoṯət? Does the apparent -i reflect plural/feminine morphology or a clitic-related variant?
At 1.6/87 and 1.49/2214 who helped whom? At 2.11/2810 does mʕawanlan mean we helped these people (as the preceding aḥna suggests), rather than the machine translation’s these people helped us?

Confirm helper/assisted-person segmentation in 1.46/2056 mʕawnili, 2.28/4652 mʕawənalli, 3.36/1022 mʕawanlelox and 4.II/686 mʕawallalan; the meaning of help is secure but person roles can be obscured by contraction.
At 2.5/1363 is ʕƏwono a productive Infinitiv in the native paradigm or a lexical aid noun? No new borrowing history is established.
Correct unterstürzen to unterstützen
rationale: In the German list helfen, beistehen, ..., verhelfen, the intended verb unterstützen has been misspelled unterstürzen.

summary: The tongue helps the teeth: an inanimate helper and inanimate assisted participants retain the ordinary helping relation

The ordinary helper relation extends to a government, military force, funeral household, liturgical service and intercession before Christ. Intercessors are helpers in a religious domain, not a new sense of the verb.
